src/app/GitUI/CommandsDialogs/FormBrowse.notes: Functional repository shell with the implemented Repository/Commands/Tools menus and upstream-shaped ToolStripMain/ToolStripFilters chrome. The same FormBrowse instance switches between the Dashboard and repository panes when the working directory becomes invalid or valid; Dashboard selections and Open/Close commands use that boundary rather than creating a second shell. The first loaded repository host owns the same-named top-level menu; fork/clone remains available outside a repository, while view/create pull request and add-upstream resolve the provider relevant to the current repository and preserve the original errors and command boundaries. The compact 25px toolbar has refresh/left-panel/lower-workspace layout controls, worktree manager/switcher, the same-named searchable favourite/recent working-directory split selector, current-branch selector, persisted pull split actions, push/commit/stash actions, file explorer, terminal, configured user scripts, and the live Settings host; it wraps rather than hiding commands at narrow widths. The working-directory selector routes open/close and Ctrl-new-instance actions through the original command IDs, records the valid recent working directory once, and opens the native recent-repository settings twin. One same-named GitStatusMonitor status result drives the configurable Commit state/count and artificial-revision counters, while the existing ahead/behind provider drives the same-named Push button's arrow/count text with repository/branch stale-result rejection. The worktree split contribution appears only when more than one worktree exists and reuses the original create/prune/manage and current/deleted-row behavior. The original CommitInfoTabControl boundary hosts selection-driven Commit and Diff, lazily loaded File tree and GPG, a lazy portable plain-text shell, shared Output history, and the selection-driven Build Report contribution when build-server data exists; Output follows the original tab-versus-toggleable-panel settings. ShowSplitViewLayout and below/left/right CommitInfoPosition settings are shared with WinForms, and in-session splitter sizes survive toggling/position changes. The shared submodule-status provider now refreshes the left-panel hierarchy and is canceled with repository changes/shutdown. Portable plugins load and register through the original lifecycle, including unregister/re-register on repository changes; the Browse menu lists them alphabetically, materializes their embedded portable PNGs, executes them through the original GitUIEventArgs boundary, and routes its settings command to the Plugins root. Browse hotkeys dispatch the implemented commands and workspace focus/navigation with upstream IDs, including OpenRepo Ctrl+O, CloseRepository Ctrl+W, and ManageWorkTrees ID 49; configured user-script hotkeys retain the original Scripts category and command IDs, the original QuickFetch ID 11 runs before/after fetch event scripts, Ctrl+D6 and Ctrl+D9 focus Console and Output, while F5 uses Avalonia-only command ID 50 because WinForms routes it through ToolStrip shortcut handling. The selected Diff/File tree supplies selected paths and caret position through the original script-options provider boundary. The revision grid receives the shared ahead/behind provider and quick filter state; its path filter supplies the same followed-file fallback to both RevisionDiffControl instances. The upstream BrowseArguments constructor now applies revision/path filters, requested selection, and file-history left-panel mode before the initial asynchronous load. Repository reload, refs/history, worktrees, submodules, GPG, build-server polling, and plugin discovery work use owned lifetime boundaries, so queued notifications and unfinished providers cannot outlive shutdown. The Help menu exposes the original check-for-updates contribution, and the weekly startup check is routed through an injected production-only update service so view tests never contact the network. Main panes preserve invisible 6px splitter drag targets, adjacent 1px borders, 6px content padding, and the 260px repository-tree distance. The headless-Skia harness captures the complete shell in light/dark at 100%/125%/150%/200% scaling. Design-time construction uses an isolated TaskManager because the previewer runs before ThreadHelper initialization.
